div.p: Bearings rarely fail alone. Seals protect them — oil, shaft and hydraulic seals matched on bore, material and profile go out on the same order as the bearing they are protecting.

div.h2: How to read a bearing part number
div.p: A bearing number is a base designation plus prefixes and suffixes. The base tells you the type and the bore; the suffixes tell you how the bearing is closed and how much internal clearance it has. Two suffixes that answer two different questions — do not read one as the other.

div.h3: Seals and shields — the closure suffix

tr.td: Clean environments, or oil circulation / external sealing
Dust, moderate speed, low drag. Grease retained for life
Moisture and fine contamination on one face
Washdown, humidity, fine dust. Best ingress protection of the four

div.p: A metal shield seals by a narrow gap and adds almost no drag. A rubber seal rubs the rotating ring, so it protects better but costs a little friction and speed rating. That is the trade.

tr.td: Heat from the fit, or thermal expansion in service
Heavy interference fits and elevated running temperature

div.p: Clearance and closure combine freely. A 6205-2RS-C3 is a 6205 size bearing, rubber sealed both sides, running looser than normal clearance — a very common press or motor choice.

div.h2: Cross-brand equivalents — the same part, different letters
div.p: Every manufacturer uses its own letters for identical function. This is where most ordering errors start, and where a brand-agnostic distributor earns its keep.

div.h3: What is the difference between 2RS and ZZ bearings?
div.p: 2RS means a rubber seal on both sides, contacting the rotating ring. ZZ means a metal shield on both sides, non-contacting. Choose 2RS for moisture and fine contamination, ZZ for dust and higher speed with lower friction.
div.h3: Which bearing clearance should I specify?
div.p: Normal clearance suits most applications. Specify C3 where the bearing runs hot from the fit or from thermal expansion in service, which is why C3 is common in electric motors and pumps. C2 is for precision work where runout must stay tight.
